#Part A — Creating Vectors and List:
Question 1
```{r}
#A. Create a vector for the worker’s age.
worker_age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41, 48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)

#B. How many data points?
length(worker_age)
# Output: 50

#C. Find the minimum and the maximum value of worker's age
# Minimum
min(worker_age)
# Output: 17

# Maximum
max(worker_age)
# Output: 61

# Alternatively, both at once:
range(worker_age)

#D. Access the 13th to 18th elements and 33rd to 35th elements of worker's Age
worker_age[c(13:18, 33:35)]
# Output: 27 22 37 34 19 20 33 41 53

#E. Access all but the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th elements are not included
worker_age[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]

#F. Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0
worker_age[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0

# Check the modified vector:
worker_age
```
Question #2
```{r}
data(rivers)
#A. Get the number of elements (length) in rivers, their sum (sum), mean (mean), median(median), variance(var), standard deviation(sd), minimum (min) and maximum (max).
# Create a single named vector containing all the calculated summary values
river_stats <- c(
  Length = length(rivers),
  Sum = sum(rivers),
  Mean = mean(rivers),
  Median = median(rivers),
  Variance = var(rivers),
  SD = sd(rivers),
  Min = min(rivers),
  Max = max(rivers)
)

# Display the vector
river_stats

#B. Output Result
#Answer: 
#Length          Sum         Mean       Median     Variance           SD 
  #141.000000 83357.000000   591.184397   425.000000 243908.408652   493.870842 
         #Min          Max 
  #Min 135.000000  Max 3710.000000
  
```
Question #3:
```{r}
#A. Create vectors according to the above table
power_ranking <- 1:25

celebrity_name <- c(
  "Tom Cruise", "Rolling Stones", "Oprah Winfrey", "U2", "Tiger Woods",
  "Steven Spielberg", "Howard Stern", "50 Cent", "Cast of the Sopranos", "Dan Brown",
  "Bruce Springsteen", "Donald Trump", "Muhammad Ali", "Paul McCartney", "George Lucas",
  "Elton John", "David Letterman", "Phil Mickelson", "J.K Rowling", "Bradd Pitt",
  "Peter Jackson", "Dr. Phil McGraw", "Jay Lenon", "Celine Dion", "Kobe Bryant"
)

pay <- c(
  67, 90, 225, 110, 90,
  332, 302, 41, 52, 88,
  55, 44, 55, 40, 233,
  34, 40, 47, 75, 25,
  39, 45, 32, 40, 31
)

#B. Modify the power ranking and pay of J.K. Rowling. Change power ranking to 15 and pay to 90
# Find the index of J.K Rowling
jk_index <- which(celebrity_name == "J.K Rowling")  # Index 19

# Modify power ranking and pay
power_ranking[jk_index] <- 15
pay[jk_index] <- 90

# Verify updates
power_ranking[jk_index]
pay[jk_index]
```
Question #4
```{r}
vegetables <- c("Carrot", "Broccoli", "Spinach", "Potato", "Tomato", "Cabbage", "Onion", "Garlic", "Cucumber", "Eggplant")
vegetables
#A. Add 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetables in the list. What is the result?
vegetables <- c(vegetables, "Pumpkin", "Zucchini")
vegetables
# Result: "Carrot" "Broccoli" "Spinach" "Potato" "Tomato" "Cabbage" "Onion" "Garlic" "Cucumber" "Eggplant" "Pumpkin" "Zucchini"

#B. How many datapoints do you have?
length(vegetables)
# Output: 12

#C. Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5. What is the result?
new_veggies <- c("Cauliflower", "Lettuce", "Asparagus", "Celery")
vegetables <- append(vegetables, new_veggies, after = 5)
vegetables
# Result: "Carrot" "Broccoli" "Spinach" "Potato" "Tomato" "Cauliflower" "Lettuce" "Asparagus" "Celery" "Cabbage" "Onion" "Garlic" "Cucumber" "Eggplant" "Pumpkin" "Zucchini"

#D. How many datapoints does your vegetable list have?
length(vegetables)
# Output: 16
```
